query: Consider the following context: Constituent phases and their corresponding phase transformations are important in developing alloys. In that context, which method can be used for control of phase evolution in Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni HEAs, and why?

generation.hypothesis: The formation and evolution of phases in Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni High-Entropy Alloys (HEAs) can be controlled through the manipulation of alloy composition and processing conditions.
generation.material_initial_state: Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni HEA in its initial, unprocessed state
generation.intervention: Adjustment of alloy composition and processing conditions
generation.conditions: Varied composition ratios of the constituent elements and different processing techniques such as casting, forging, or heat treatment
generation.mechanism: Thermodynamic and kinetic factors influencing phase stability and evolution
generation.predicted_outcome: Controlled phase evolution leading to tailored microstructures and properties
generation.baseline: Uncontrolled phase evolution in the as-cast or as-forged state
generation.boundary: Limits of compositional and processing condition variations that still allow for the formation of a high-entropy alloy
generation.uncertainty: Insufficient data on specific compositional and processing condition effects on phase evolution in Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni HEAs

falsification_experiment.design: Systematic variation of composition and processing conditions to observe phase evolution
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If no correlation between composition/processing conditions and phase evolution is observed, the hypothesis is falsified
